newsitem.title: USA: Noven gets SUNY anti-cavity license.
newsitem.headline: Noven gets SUNY anti-cavity license.

text.p: Noven Pharmaceuticals Inc and SUNY Stony Brook said Thursday that the Research Foundation of the State University of New York has granted an exclusive worldwide license to Noven for the use of a new generation of anti-cavity compounds.
They said that the Research Foundation has entered into a separate research agreement whereby Noven would fund the clinical and commercial development of these compounds.

Cavities or tooth decay occur when sugars and other fermentable carbohydrates in the diet are broken down by bacteria in the mouth to form acid which then dissolves the structural mineral of the tooth, hydroxyapatite.
According to Noven and the university, until now, fluoride has been the main cavity fighter making teeth more resistant to dissolution by bacterial acids.
They said that these new compounds developed at Stony Brook are comprised of natural elements that protect the tooth from dissolving and provide the powerful cavity-fighting protection of saliva.
